WELCOME TO CHESTNUT GROVE
Based in Balham, south London, Chestnut Grove Academy is a co-educational secondary school for 11 to 19-year olds with an excellent Sixth Form. Part of the Wandle Learning Trust, the school has been rated 'good' by Ofsted since 2019. Click on the video link right to learn more about us and our creative learning community.

British values
Chestnut Grove Academy is a rights-respecting school. Our PROUD values are underpinned by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. This means that we are committed to teaching our students about rights through rights-respecting language and practices. We also encourage all our students to be ambassadors: acting as advocates for the rights of others.
Our resources are award-winning: in 2016, the school was awarded the Accord Inclusivity Award as well as the Educate and Celebrate LGBT+ Gold Best Practice Status Award. In particular, the school was praised for tackling controversial and sensitive issues head-on as well as its commitment to human rights, fundamental British values and Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development (SMSC). We have also been awarded the Gold Equalities Award and the UNICEF Silver Award and are currently working towards the Carnegie Anti-Racism Award. We are far from perfect but working towards these awards ensures that equality and human rights are always a top priority.
Learning about rights
Human rights are mapped across all the curricula of the school, and students are taught the many rights of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. For example, in Health, students focus on one particular right in every lesson, such as the right to health, life or education. All of our subjects address Article 2 – the right to non-discrimination – by considering how different groups are represented in the curriculum. Our commitment to addressing race, gender, disability and LGBT+ issues is mapped in our Equalities and Human Rights Map. Full details of how human rights and equality are addressed in the curriculum can be found in our Curriculum Guides.
Learning through rights
Being a rights-respecting school also means ensuring that our policies and practices are underpinned by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Our school charter was written by students and we expect all students and staff to follow it. The school also uses restorative justice and resolution to deal with behavioural issues that arise, and students are taught from Year 7 how to do this effectively.
UNICEF ambassadors
Our students are all encouraged to take part in charity work and learn about the many ways they can help those who cannot access their rights. Students who wish to can join our Equality and Human Rights Club, which meets weekly and works on a range of campaigns each term. Students also feedback on areas of concern and, alongside the School Council, work with the student body to ensure their voices are heard. For further details, please email Ms Taylor-Campbell.

The Chestnut Grove curriculum provides a rigorous, knowledge-rich, transformational education, encapsulated through our PROUD values, which prepares our students to succeed at university, thrive in employment and lead fulfilling lives. It is the embodiment of our ethos of a creative learning community, which marries traditional and dynamic approaches to teaching and learning.

PROUD values
As an Academy, we respect the rights of students, their families and our staff. We believe that everybody is entitled to receive the best education. As a creative learning community, we are committed to ensuring that everyone develops through praise, encouragement, rigour and structure. Central to this are the PROUD values – Positive, Resilient, Open-minded, Unified and Determined – which are how we convey the Academy’s ethos to our students.
We expect every student and member of staff to follow the Community Charter written by our students.

Welcome to the Sixth Form
A welcome from the Sixth Form Team
At Chestnut Grove Academy, we are proud of our students’ achievements and of our tradition of excellence. Our moral purpose is to foster a lifelong love of learning, to stimulate intellectual curiosity and to develop independence within our student body. We achieve this through exceptional teaching and learning opportunities, both within and beyond the classroom, and through our provision of outstanding advice, information and guidance.
We consider each student not only as an individual but also as a two-year project to help them into the university, apprenticeship or a career of their choice. Our inclusive ethos encourages students to participate and contribute to the vibrancy of the school and to the wider local community. Our enrichment, enhancement and extra-curricular provision is purposely designed to broaden the student experience and to challenge our students to think critically and to problem-solve. Our aim is student personal development in all its forms.
A strong induction programme supports the transition from Key Stage 4 into Key Stage 5 and enables all our students to access appropriate pathways to unlock their potential, allowing them to progress and succeed. Students leave us as mature young adults, equipped with the essential life skills necessary to face a rapidly changing world.
Chestnut Grove is an open access school sixth form, meaning applicants are welcome to join us from other schools and colleges provided that they meet the entry requirements for our post-16 courses and pathways. Each year we receive many applications from external students and external applicants can be assured of a smooth transition, something which will enable them to quickly feel part of the Chestnut Grove community.
Chestnut Grove Sixth Form provides a rich and varied curriculum and enrichment, with excellent outcomes, in an environment that is both challenging and supportive. Sixth formers inspire younger students through a range of student leadership opportunities, and student voice is threaded throughout. We look forward to welcoming you into the sixth form!
For more information on our Sixth Form offer, view our Sixth Form prospectus.

Art and Languages Specialist Programme
Art Specialist Programme:
The Art specialist programme at CGA offers a dedicated pathway for students in each KS3 year group who have successfully secured a place through the selection process. Those chosen as Art Specialists attend an additional timetabled lesson each week, where they explore a wide range of materials, techniques and creative approaches that go beyond the core curriculum, helping to stretch and challenge their artistic abilities.
Lessons are taught in a hands-on, exploratory way, encouraging experimentation, independence and the development of a personal style. Throughout the year, students also benefit from exciting opportunities such as using specialist equipment, working with visiting artists and taking on a mini-GCSE style project.
The programme is open to all applicants who are willing to take part in the selection process, which involves attending a designated assessment day where students complete a practical task assessed by the Art Department. Anyone is welcome to apply, but if you enjoy being creative, experimenting with new ideas and expressing yourself through art, this is the programme for you.
You can also get a glimpse of what to expect through photos from previous years, showcasing students’ work, activities and trips.
Language Specialist Programme
The Languages Specialist Programme offers students the opportunity to broaden their linguistic and cultural knowledge through an engaging and structured learning experience.
From Years 7 to 9, students receive one additional lesson per week, during which they learn Italian from scratch while also exploring aspects of Italian culture such as food, film, and festivals. Lessons follow a grammar-based scheme of work designed to prepare students for the GCSE course in Key Stage 4, with sessions taking place either before school or during period 6 in KS3, and becoming part of the regular timetable in Years 10 and 11.
Beyond the classroom, students benefit from a variety of enrichment activities, including cookery sessions, museum visits, and the highlight- the trip to Rome in Years 8 and 9. The programme is open to all students, but is particularly well-suited to those with an interest in languages and a curiosity about different cultures and traditions.

pageCache.text:
Careers Programme
At Chestnut Grove Academy, we aim for our students to leave school with a careers education that has helped raise their aspirations and give them the skills to ensure that they succeed at university, thrive in employment and lead fulfilling lives, in line with our Curriculum Intent.
We ensure all pupils, from Year 7 upwards, are kept fully up to date with the most recent careers information, so that they can make well-informed decisions about their next steps after Chestnut Grove Academy.
CHOICES MAGAZINE - INSPIRING CAREERS PROGRAMME
Apprenticeships
Explaining Apprenticeships
Our careers programme
Our careers strategy is developed in line with the Gatsby Benchmarks of Good Career Guidance and the Baker Clause, which states that schools must allow colleges and training providers access to every student in Years 8 to 13 to discuss non-academic routes.
Careers are an integrated part of our curriculum. All subject areas make reference to and discuss career opportunities specific to individual areas, as well as exploring the transferable skills which enable pupils to develop across all year groups. In addition, we also employ an independent careers advisor who meets with students on a one-to-one basis to offer additional support.
Pupils with SEND are further supported by staff in Learning Support and our school SENCO liaises with our Careers Leader and additional outside agencies for pupils as necessary.
Other careers education, information advice and guidance (CIEAG) activities we offer include:
Information and research activities
Visits to work places
Peer mentor sessions
Workshops on a variety of career topics
Mock interview sessions
CV and personal statement sessions
Careers education in the curriculum
Key Stage 3The aim of careers education in Key Stage 3 is to introduce pupils to the working world, the vocabulary associated with it, and the wide range of possible careers that they could pursue. They will start thinking about what they personally would want from a career, and will start to develop their skills on how to investigate careers further. They will think about critical employability skills or qualifications that would be needed for different careers, and through identifying their own personal traits, strengths and skills, will start to develop a long term action plan. At the end of Key Stage 3, pupils will be encouraged to use the careers resources they have been introduced to, to help inform their GCSE decisions. In line with the Baker Clause, students will be made aware of a wide range of qualifications available for them; academic, creative, vocational and technical.
In Key Stage 4, the emphasis shifts onto preparing pupils for making their post-16 choices, and for the world of work; into which they may shortly be entering. They will learn about A-level subjects and what they involve, but will also be informed about all other possible options available to them after their GCSEs, including colleges, technical colleges, and apprenticeships. To prepare them for employment, pupils will focus more on CV and interview skills, and will learn about their rights and responsibilities, budgeting and payslips. They are encouraged to investigate potential career paths further, and will use this information, together with advice and research to help inform their post-16 decisions. In line with the Baker Clause, students will be made aware of a wide range of qualifications available for them; academic, creative, vocational and technical.
In Key Stage 5 we aim to prepare pupils for making their post-18 choices, and for becoming an independent adult. They will learn about all the options that are available to them, including higher education, jobs, gap years and apprenticeships, and given assistance on whichever route they choose to go down. Students are given advice on writing personal statements, with emphasis on UCAS, apprenticeship and job applications, and they will receive a lot of support on interview preparation, leading up to a mock interview day. To help further with their transition to university and adult life they learn about study skills, student finance and budgeting. We believe that developing employability skills is very important, so encourage pupils to take part in work experience. In line with the Baker Clause, students will be made aware of a wide range of qualifications available for them; academic, creative, vocational and technical.
Measuring impact
Chestnut Grove Academy uses internally and externally produced reports to assess the impact of our careers education, information, advice and guidance. The Department for Education Destination Measures report enables us to see how many students remain in education, employment or training at post 16 compared to other schools in Wandsworth and nationally.
We also use the Careers and Enterprise Company ‘compass too’l to evaluate our provision and assess whether we are meeting the 8 recommended Gatsby Benchmarks. This report is run every 3 months. Students evaluate careers activities such as the Careers Fair and their individual careers appointments through student voice feedback forms.
Application for provider access
Chestnut Grove Academy provides the opportunity for providers to come into the school and support students on a range of opportunities in Further and Higher Institutions and Apprenticeships.
If you are an employer and feel that you could help our students experience the world of work, please get in touch with Rachael Robinson, Assistant Headteacher / Careers Lead via e-mail: rrobinson@chestnutgrove.org.uk
Careers information for employers, parents and students
Please visit our Academy Policies page to read our Careers Education, Impartial Advice and Guidance Policy.

Welcome from the Executive Headteacher and the Head of School
Welcome to our Creative Learning Community
When students join Chestnut Grove Academy, they are welcomed into a high-achieving, forward-thinking, caring community. Our ethos is characterised by a strong tradition of academic rigour and a thirst for creativity in every aspect of our curriculum. We feel passionately that this is a winning combination.
We are justifiably proud of our students’ achievements. They are talented, ambitious and resilient and this has secured examination results which continue to go from strength to strength. We achieve this through exceptionally high expectations. Teachers develop positive relationships with their students which nurture academic achievement and prepare students to lead fulfilling lives.
Chestnut Grove prides itself on being a happy and vibrant place to learn. We firmly believe that students achieve when they feel the genuine security of a community that supports learning and promotes social responsibility.
We work closely with parents as we believe that educating your child is a joint effort between home and school. We will involve you fully in what your child is studying, how they are performing and their targets for further progress. I am incredibly proud of our exceptionally talented staff who will get the very best out of your child both academically and through the wide range of extra-curricular activities they offer. Together, we will succeed in fulfilling your child’s potential.
Christian KingsleyExecutive Headteacher
At Chestnut Grove, we are proud to offer a knowledge-rich and academically rigorous curriculum that consistently enables our students to achieve outstanding results. However, our vision extends beyond academic excellence: we are deeply committed to nurturing healthy, happy, curious and intellectually agile individuals who are ready to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Our curriculum is fully rounded, with academic challenge at its core, thoughtfully balanced with a rich offer of visual and performing arts, which ensures that creativity is not only encouraged but celebrated. Alongside this, our robust pastoral curriculum empowers students to make informed choices, lead healthy lives and develop cultural awareness and social confidence.
Central to our ethos are the PROUD values, which shape every aspect of school life. These values foster not only exceptional learners but also compassionate, confident and courageous young people - ready to succeed at university, flourish in the workplace and lead fulfilling lives.
At Chestnut Grove, we believe education should inspire curiosity, creativity and confidence - and we are proud to deliver a curriculum that does just that.
Violeta FabianiHead of School

pageCache.pageTitle: UNICEF Rights Respecting - Chestnut Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
We are a UNICEF GOLD Rights Respecting School
We are a UNICEF Gold Rights Respecting School. This means that all our policies and practices are underpinned by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. We are one of very few London schools to have been honoured with the gold award. Students at Chestnut Grove Academy learn about rights in all of lessons. We believe in pluralism of perspective. This means that all protected groups are represented in our curriculum. We have worked hard to decolonise our resources and ensure they are inclusive of sex, sexuality, disability and different beliefs.
Our commitment to inclusion and equality is based on the fundamental belief that every child is deserving of an education that allows them to achieve their potential. Our students are encouraged, in all year groups, to be ambassadors, campaigning for the rights of others. Our Student Council, Equality Group and other working parties, ensure that pupil, staff and parent participation drives school improvement. In recent years, our students have transformed the catering offer across the school and raised hundreds of pounds for the annual UNICEF appeal.

Learning Resources
School Library
The school library, located on the ground floor of the North Building, is the beating heart of the school. Our dedicated full-time librarian is on hand throughout the day to support students with locating resources and immersing themselves in a world of books, which are regularly updated on student and staff recommendation. The library is open from 8.30am until 4pm every day.
Teams
Chestnut Grove uses the online learning platform Teams to create a virtual learning space which can be accessed both in school and at home. All students have access to Microsoft Office and its suite of programmes to support their learning. As well as being used to set home learning assignments, class teams are used by teachers to share useful resources and links for further reading.
GCSEPod
GCSEPod is a resource to help students learn, retain and recall all the information they need to do their homework, revise and achieve their GCSE goals. It comprises one website, three apps and more than 6,000 Pods (or videos) which provide audio-visual learning in short three to five-minute chunks. Click on the links below for more information:
For details of other learning resources for a specific subject, visit the Curriculum by subject page.
